title: Option value pipeline: argv string -> typed callback kwarg
answers: How does --count 3 become an int in the callback?
Where do type conversion, defaults and envvar lookup happen in click?
What is the call order from Command.main to the callback?
body:
NOTE (kind=callpath) "Option value pipeline: argv string -> typed callback kwarg"
Flow (src/click):
- core.py:Command.main -> Command.make_context -> Command.parse_args (drives parsing + per-param processing).
- core.py:Command.make_parser -> Option.add_to_parser registers each param with parser.py's option parser; parser.py:parse_args / _process_args_for_options / _process_opts / _match_long_opt / _match_short_opt / _get_value_from_state pull raw strings; parser.py:_Option.process stores raw value in state.opts[dest] (actions store/append/count; count just increments an int).
- Back in parse_args, params are handled in order from core.py:iter_params_for_processing; each calls Parameter.handle_parse_result -> consume_value (source order: command line, then envvar via resolve_envvar_value, then default_map/Context.lookup_default, then get_default) -> process_value -> type_cast_value.
- Type conversion: types.py:ParamType.__call__ (skips None) -> ParamType.convert; for int: types.py:_NumberParamTypeBase.convert calls _number_class(value), fail() on ValueError.
- Envvar: core.py:Parameter.resolve_envvar_value; Option.resolve_envvar_value adds fallback to auto_envvar_prefix + '__' + NAME (double underscore).
- Defaults: core.py:Parameter.get_default / Option.get_default; no type cast at get_default time (8.0.2), cast happens later in process_value.
- Callback: Command.invoke -> Context.invoke(callback, **ctx.params).

history.reason: The envvar template in Option.resolve_envvar_value has changed from single to double underscore. The current code shows `f"{ctx.auto_envvar_prefix}__{self.name.upper()}"` but the note claims it uses `auto_envvar_prefix + '_' + NAME`. This is a concrete technical detail that changed.
